newsitem.title: USA: Phillips-Van Heusen sees $1.31/shr Q2 charge.
newsitem.headline: Phillips-Van Heusen sees $1.31/shr Q2 charge.

text.p: Phillips-Van Heusen Corp said Thursday that it will take a non-recurring pre-tax charge in the second quarter, ending August 3, of $55 million, or $33.5 million ($1.31 per share) after taxes, reflecting accelerated restructuring activity.
As part of the restructuring, between 450 and 500 jobs will be cut, the company said.

Phillips-Van Heusen said it plans to close 150 of its retail stores and will exit the sweater manufacturing business, which operates from a plant in Puerto Rico. The sweater business loses $2 million a year, it said.
Phillips-Van Heusen also said that it would close down its Atlanta distribution facility to reduce costs.

The company said that the overall effect of the restructuring will be cash positive by fiscal year 1998 and that these actions will allow it to build its core brands such as Gant, while contracting its retailing business.
The company added, however, that it does plan to open a Gant Flagship Store on Fifth Avenue in New York City this fall. The Gant brand has performed well, it said, in Europe and Asia.
